brief.scope: the change on lane/effort-per-role against dev: effort forwarded to three CLIs, per-job model and effort resolution in the dispatcher, a new security-audit job, and the review fan-out; a first work order through the loop

findings.claim: The unvalidated job name enters Bash indirect expansion. Array-subscript command substitutions are evaluated before jobs.json validation, permitting arbitrary host commands even during --dry-run.
findings.reproduce: C=-c PAYLOAD='printf "INDIRECT_EXECUTED\n" >&2' LAUNCHER_PIN=ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py bash ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh --job 'x[$(${BASH} ${C} "${PAYLOAD}")]' --harness codex --scope-file ops/devlane/infra/secrets/README.md --worktree . --dry-run

findings.claim: security-audit declares a read-only role, but Codex receives workspace-write. Snapshot modifications by a read role are recorded but do not invalidate an approving envelope, allowing the auditor to alter its evidence.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'import json; j=json.load(open("ops/devlane/task/jobs.json"))["security-audit"]; print(j["role"], j["constraints"])' && sed -n '166,174p;1080,1103p' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py

findings.claim: The new effort evidence validator accepts any token merely containing the requested effort and never compares effort_argv with harness.argv. A record claiming xhigh therefore validates even when no effort option reached the CLI.
findings.reproduce: cd ops/devlane/dispatch/tests && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c 'from test_record import _RecordCase; c=_RecordCase("runTest"); r=c.built(); r["model"]["effort_requested"]="xhigh"; r["model"]["effort_argv"]=["not-xhigh"]; r["harness"]["argv"]=["codex","exec","--model","M"]; v=c.recmod().validate(r); print(v["model"]["effort_argv"], v["harness"]["argv"])'

findings.claim: The launcher accepts security-audit results without checking the effort reported by the vendor stream. Codex turn_context and Grok summaries expose actual effort, but _stream ignores both, so a silently downgraded security audit remains valid.
The new security gate is assigned to the floating gpt-daybreak-blue-latest alias. Its implementation can change without a repository diff or immutable version pin.

envelope.note: Read all 1,816 diff lines and inspected the changed tree. Shell/argv, permissions, vendor evidence, secrets, paths/refs, templates, SQL, and supply-chain surfaces were covered. Secret scan was clean across 19 changed tracked files; no SQL or dependency/lock/action changes were present. ../in contained no files, so there were no named inputs there; the named diff under ../context was read whole. Live vendor execution, network behavior, and destructive containment probes were not covered.
